title: Countably closed forcing and CH

based_on.title: Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 37–38 (§12, Definition 12.1 and Lemmas 12.2–12.4; the no-new-sequences argument is supplied in full)

summary: Use internal countable closure to preserve all countable ordinal sequences, then force CH by listing old reals in countable blocks of a longer generic sequence.
abstract: A new listing can make an old set smaller without changing any of its members. Starting with a countable transitive model of ZFC, countably closed forcing prevents new countable sequences of ordinals: successive coordinate decisions have one common strengthening, and a dense-set argument makes a generic filter use such a decision. The reals and the first uncountable ordinal are consequently unchanged. A longer generic binary sequence can nevertheless be added. Conditions on countable initial segments can place each old real into one of its countable blocks, producing an extension in which the continuum hypothesis holds. If the old continuum was larger, its cardinal collapses because the same reals have acquired a shorter listing.
